content.text: Using Excalidraw, create a closed chain of 10 identical circular ellipses (circles) linked together (by overlapping them) to form a closed circular chain. The ellipses stroke color should be exactly #C0C0C0 (silver).
I'll help you create a closed chain of 10 circles in Excalidraw. Let me start by taking a screenshot to see the current state.

I can see the Excalidraw canvas. Let me plan this out. I need to create 10 circles arranged in a big circle, overlapping each other to form a closed chain.

Let me first draw one circle to understand the properties and set the stroke color. Let me select the ellipse tool.
The ellipse tool is selected and the properties panel is showing. Let me first set the stroke color to #C0C0C0. I'll click on the stroke color swatch to open the color picker.
The color picker is open with a hex code field showing "1e1e1e". Let me clear it and type the new hex code. I'll triple-click to select all the text in the field.

The triple-click didn't select the existing text - it appended. The hex code now shows "1e1e1ec0c0c0" which is wrong. Let me clear the field properly. Let me click in the field and select all with keyboard.
Browser action failed: Keyboard.press: Unknown key: "ctrl"
The field is now empty. Let me type the correct hex code.

The hex code now shows "c0c0c0" and the stroke color swatch shows silver/gray. Now let me close the color picker by clicking elsewhere and start drawing the circles.

Let me plan the geometry. I'll create 10 circles arranged around a big circle. For a closed chain, consecutive circles must overlap. 

Let me calculate positions. I'll use a center at (700, 430) with a chain radius R. Each circle has diameter d. For 10 circles evenly spaced around a circle of radius R, the distance between adjacent centers is 2·R·sin(π/10) = 2·R·sin(18°) = 2·R·0.309 = 0.618·R. For overlap, the diameter d must be greater than this distance. 

Let me use R = 200, so center distance = 123.6. Let me use diameter = 150 (radius 75), so they overlap nicely.

Let me compute the 10 center positions (angle = 36° increments):

Now let me calculate the 10 circle positions. Center of chain: (700, 430), R = 200, circle diameter = 150 (so radius 75).

For each circle i (i=0 to 9), angle = i × 36°:
- Center x = 700 + 200·cos(angle)
- Center y = 430 + 200·sin(angle)
- Top-left = center - 75, Bottom-right = center + 75

Let me compute:
- i=0 (0°): center (900, 430) → TL(825,355) BR(975,505)
- i=1 (36°): center (700+161.8, 430+117.6)=(861.8, 547.6) → TL(786.8,472.6) BR(936.8,622.6)
- i=2 (72°): center (700+61.8, 430+190.2)=(761.8, 620.2) → TL(686.8,545.2) BR(836.8,695.2)
- i=3 (108°): center (700-61.8, 430+190.2)=(638.2, 620.2) → TL(563.2,545.2) BR(713.2,695.2)
- i=4 (144°): center (700-161.8, 430+117.6)=(538.2, 547.6) → TL(463.2,472.6) BR(613.2,622.6)
- i=5 (180°): center (500, 430) → TL(425,355) BR(575,505)
- i=6 (216°): center (538.2, 312.4) → TL(463.2,237.4) BR(613.2,387.4)
- i=7 (252°): center (638.2, 239.8) → TL(563.2,164.8) BR(713.2,314.8)
- i=8 (288°): center (761.8, 239.8) → TL(686.8,164.8) BR(836.8,314.8)
- i=9 (324°): center (861.8, 312.4) → TL(786.8,237.4) BR(936.8,387.4)

Some of these go near the top toolbar (y=165 for i=7,8). The toolbar is around y=20-60, so y=165 should be fine. Let me start drawing. I'll draw each circle by dragging from TL to BR. First, I need to select the ellipse tool each time (it deselects after drawing). Let me draw circle 0.

The first circle is drawn with the silver stroke color. It looks good. Now the tool switched back to select. I'll need to reselect the ellipse tool for each circle. Let me draw circle 1. I'll press '4' or 'o' to select the ellipse tool.

Excellent! Five circles are drawn and they form the bottom half of the chain, overlapping nicely. The chain shape is forming well. Now let me continue with circles 6-9 (the top half). Circle 6: TL(463,237) BR(613,387).

All 10 circles are now drawn, forming a beautiful closed circular chain. Each circle overlaps with its adjacent neighbors, creating a linked chain effect. Let me click on an empty area to deselect and see the final result clearly.

The closed chain of 10 circles is complete. The result shows exactly what was requested:

✅ **10 identical circular ellipses** – all drawn with the same 150×150 pixel diameter, making them perfect circles of equal size.

✅ **Linked together by overlapping** – each circle overlaps with both of its adjacent neighbors, creating the interlocking chain-link effect.

✅ **Closed circular chain** – the circles are arranged evenly around a central point (36° apart), so the chain loops back on itself, forming a complete closed ring.

✅ **Stroke color #C0C0C0 (silver)** – I set the exact hex code `C0C0C0` in the color picker before drawing, so every circle has the silver stroke.

The chain forms a clean, symmetric ring where each circle connects seamlessly to the next, completing a full closed loop back to the starting circle.
